answeredReviewRound5: Important (the reviewer's withdrawal of its own round-4 request): sessionDeliveryOutcome.carrying no longer keeps an earlier pass's consumer for a serving-port pass that could be given none. That branch wrote the session entry as consumer delivery while the consumer's filter was an earlier plan's, which the row the registration stored disagrees with, so the relay would have served the session from a filter naming topics the row does not. Only the gap is carried now.

The tester's TestSessionConsumerKeepsAServingPortsConsumerWhenALaterPassIsRefused is turned around as TestSessionConsumerServingPortAnswersNoConsumerWhenALaterPassIsRefused, and states what the answer is rather than what it is not: no delivery field at all, no consumer delivery on the entry, the stored row the unsubscribe left, and the consumer the first pass created still on the server, for the session's next registration to re-filter — nothing claims it meanwhile, since the entry says the port is the path.
Minor: the exhaustion case asserts the literal three plans rather than registrationPlanAttempts, so raising the bound is a decision someone takes again.
Minor: carrying's doc names registerSession, which is the function that re-plans, not subscribeHandler.
Minor: the gap claim is narrowed to what the code keeps — within one registration's passes, since a later registration finds the consumer and is told no gap.
forwardMerge: GitHub reported the pull request CONFLICTING against main at 667d0737, which is the trigger. main carries two things through this change's own files: an explicit msgID on every forward (RequestCoreTo, StartRequestCoreTo, StartRequestStoredTo, forwardRole, roleForward.msgID), and a reworked publish window (WindowUntil, Request, ErrPublishUnconfirmed exported, ErrNotCaptured, ConnectionChanged).

Fourteen files conflicted. The merged forwardRole is func(subject string, item contracts.Envelope, msgID string, timeout time.Duration): main's msgID in, this change's storedOnly out, since every forward is stored-only. StartRequestStoredTo takes msgID and stamps Nats-Msg-Id only when it is not empty; everything this change deletes stays deleted.

bus.ErrReceiptTimeout is restored, in async.go beside main's new window.Request, which is its only caller now. This change deleted it with the receipt path; main grew a user of it that has nothing to do with role forwards, and its doc says so.

Two tests main added needed adapting rather than taking: delivery_role_forward_test.go forwarded with RequestCoreTo (now StartRequestStoredTo and its Wait, with everything it pins about roleForward.msgID kept), and connection_changed_test.go published with PublishCore (now PublishCoreContext).

One test main added is deleted: confirmed_test.go's TestPublishRouteStoresOneCopyOfARoleMessageItForwardsTwice drove a second forward by having the holder's stand-in withhold its first receipt, and after this change no forward waits for a receipt, so that second forward cannot happen. The property it pinned, one stored copy per message and recipient under one Nats-Msg-Id, is pinned by delivery_role_forward_test.go and by internal/bus/stored_forward_test.go.
main's own deletion of TestAWindowWithSeveralDenialsConfirmsEveryGrantedSend, which went with its window rework, is taken.

discoveredComplexity: A deletion is only as settled as the branch it was made on: this change deleted a sentinel, a publish helper and a forward API that main then grew new callers of, and each showed up as a build failure rather than as a conflict. The merge's real work was deciding, for each, whether main's new caller is of the thing that was deleted or of something that merely shares its name.
